question.problem: Find the equation of the level surface for the function $f(x,y,z)=\frac{{x}^{2}}{2{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-{z}^{2}}$ that passes through the point $P(2,\sqrt{5},3).$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the value of the function at $P$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2,\sqrt{5},3) & =\frac{(2)^{2}}{2(2)^{2}+(\sqrt{5})^{2}-(3)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{4}{4} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the level surfaces for the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the equation

$$
f(x,y,z)=c.
$$

In our case, we're interested in $c=1.$ So, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =c \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{2{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-{z}^{2}} & =1 \\ {x}^{2} & =2{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-{z}^{2} \\ {x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-{z}^{2} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the level surface that passes through the point $P(2,\sqrt{5},3)$ is the surface ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-{z}^{2}=0.$
